newsitem.title: USA: Larson-Davis and Lucent in marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: Larson-Davis and Lucent in marketing pact.

text.p: Larson-Davis Inc said Wednesday it signed an agreement with Lucent Technologies Inc to market a device which analyzes air quality in semiconductor plants and so-called clean rooms.

The existing particle analysis market is estimated at almost $300 million annually. Because of the sensitivity and speed of this device, Larson-Davis said it expects the product ultimately to generate revenues of more than $50 million annually.
Larson-Davis will receive exclusive worldwide rights to the licensed technologies. In return, Larson-Davis will pay Lucent a one-time license fee plus a scheduled royalty fee for each unit sold.
The device will be marketed to semiconductor plants and clean rooms where minute particles hamper the subminiaturization of chips, the company said in a statement.
Larson-Davis will begin taking orders for the product in the first quarter of 1998.

The device, an advanced particle analyzing mass spectrometer, combines technologies developed by both companies. Four of Larson-Davis' patents for high-speed mass spectrometry are combined with two of Lucent's patents for high-speed particle analysis creating an advanced particle analyzer.
"This agreement paves the way for the most significant revenue growth potential in our company's history," said Brian Larson, president of Larson-Davis, in a statement.

Larson-Davis develops, makes and markets ultra-sensitive analytical instrumentation for the chemical, gas, acoustics and vibration market. Its customers include industrial companies, government and military agencies.
